definition: The markup language used to structure the content and meaning of a web page.
example:
Welcome

creates a top-level heading.

definition: The stylesheet language used to control the presentation, layout, and visual appearance of web content.
example: color: navy; changes the text color of an element.

definition: A programming language that adds behavior, logic, and interactivity to web pages.
example: A click event can run a function that opens a dialog.

definition: The Document Object Model is the browser's structured representation of an HTML document that JavaScript can read and change.
example: document.querySelector('#title') selects an element from the DOM.

definition: An Application Programming Interface is a defined way for software systems to communicate and request data or actions.
example: A weather API can provide current conditions to a web application.

definition: A lightweight text format commonly used to represent and exchange structured data.
example: {"term":"HTML","category":"HTML"}

definition: The protocol browsers and web servers use to communicate through requests and responses.
example: A browser sends an HTTP GET request when it asks a server for a page.

definition: A Uniform Resource Locator identifies the location of a resource on the web.
example: https://example.com/about.html is a URL.

definition: The Domain Name System translates human-friendly domain names into network addresses used to locate servers.
example: DNS helps a browser find the server associated with example.com.

definition: An approach to web design that allows a page to adapt its layout and content to different screen sizes and devices.
example: A three-column layout can become one column on a narrow phone screen.

definition: The practice of designing websites so people with different abilities can perceive, navigate, and use them.
example: A form label connected to its input helps people using assistive technology.

definition: Using HTML elements according to their meaning and purpose rather than choosing elements only for their visual appearance.
example: Using <nav> for navigation communicates the purpose of that content.

definition: A CSS layout system designed to arrange items efficiently along one dimension.
example: display: flex can place navigation links in a row and align them.

definition: A CSS layout system designed for arranging content in rows and columns.
example: display: grid can create a responsive glossary card layout.

definition: A browser occurrence that JavaScript can respond to, such as a click, submit, input, or key press.
example: A click event can trigger a glossary modal to open.

definition: A reusable block of code that performs a task and can receive input through parameters.
example: function greet(name) performs a greeting using the supplied name.

definition: A named place in a program for storing a value that the code can use and, when appropriate, change.
example: const userName = 'Alex'; stores a string in a constant binding.

definition: An ordered collection of values that JavaScript can process using indexes and array methods.
example: const terms = ['HTML', 'CSS', 'JavaScript']; creates an array.

definition: A browser storage mechanism that lets a website persist small amounts of string data on a user's device.
example: localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark') saves a theme preference.

definition: A browser API used to make network requests and work with responses asynchronously.
example: fetch('data/glossary.json') can request the glossary data file.
